status: PROPOSAL — every name, number and skill here is a first draft for review, not an agreed design. See DESIGN.md for the decisions this is built on.

notes: Class growth is applied on every level gained and accumulates down the tree: a Berserker gains Novice + Warrior + Berserker growth each level.
health_per_vitality is inherited from the nearest ancestor that sets it, so tier 2 classes only declare it when they change it.
Automatic growth deliberately outweighs free points, so a badly allocated hero is suboptimal but never broken.
By level 15 a hero has ~28 free points. A pure advancement needs ~8 of them; a hybrid needs ~13. That gap is what makes hybrids a deliberate commitment rather than a default.

classes.name: Novice
classes.description: Levels 1-4, before the first advancement. Grows evenly and slowly in everything, which is exactly why you want out of it.
classes.design_note: Not in DESIGN.md, which said tier 1 has no prerequisite. Adding a tier 0 makes the tree uniform, gives the classless phase an identity, and means a level 1 hero has a skill to bring into a run instead of only auto-attacking.

classes.name: Warrior
classes.description: Stands in the middle of the swarm and stays there. Highest survivability of the three, shortest reach.

classes.name: Mage
classes.description: Highest raw damage and the best crowd control, on the thinnest health pool. Punished hard for being caught.

classes.name: Ranger
classes.description: Fast attacks, fast feet. Wins by never being where the swarm is, loses when cornered.

classes.name: Berserker
classes.description: Trades the Warrior's caution for output that climbs as its health falls.

classes.name: Archmage
classes.description: Slow, enormous spells. The highest ceiling in the game and the least margin for a mistake.

classes.name: Assassin
classes.description: Deletes single targets and disengages. Struggles against density.

classes.name: Spellblade
classes.description: The sword-swinging mage. Reachable from either side: a Warrior who invested INT, or a Mage who invested STR.

classes.name: Arcane Archer
classes.description: Ranged damage that covers ground rather than pointing at one enemy.

classes.name: Duelist
classes.description: Melee that keeps moving. Weaker per hit than a Berserker, far harder to pin down.

notes: Three base classes, each with one pure advancement and access to two hybrids. Every pair of base classes shares exactly one hybrid, so the tree is a triangle rather than three isolated columns.
A hybrid lists two prerequisites, so it is reachable from either parent. DESIGN.md's single-prerequisite phrasing does not cover this — the schema needs a list.
Tier 3 is deliberately absent until the game exists.

reachability_check.notes: All three base classes grow their primary stat at the same rate, so every advancement costs the same from whichever side you approach it. That symmetry is the point: it makes the tree explainable without a spreadsheet.
reachability_check.open_question: Durability identity now rides on health_per_vitality rather than on VIT growth, because differing VIT growth was what broke the cost symmetry. Whether one field is enough to make a Mage feel fragile is untested.
